structured_output.summary: Known pulsator with -1523 ppm P/2 modulation and sector depths p 7e-14; Sectors 112-114 decide.
reasons: I agree with the mechanical decision 'held'. The step 9 run of 2026-11-02 00:52 now raises the caution 'star varies at half the period', which earlier runs recorded as a value without a caution; the two earlier agent decisions in the verification record (2026-11-01 22:18 and 22:31) reached 'held' on the same evidence.

The target itself is a known pulsator: vsx_variables lists Gaia DR3 6064573197263477376 DSCT|GDOR|SXPHE at 0". Step 9 finds ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm -1523 +/- 118 ppm (13 sigma) with the same sign in all six sectors (ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm_by_sector -1179 to -1823), and ellipsoidal_companion_mass_solar_masses is empty. A negative sign is unphysical for ellipsoidal variation and the amplitude is 1.8 times fit_depth_ppm 863, so this is most likely a gamma Dor or delta Scuti mode near 2/P locked to the search period. A pulsation-driven false alarm at period_days 0.735052 is therefore a real possibility that none of the steps models (TRICERATOPS tests only astrophysical false positives).

The per-sector depths from the QLP light curves are inconsistent: sector_depth_consistency_p_value 7.08e-14, with depth_ppm_by_sector running from S102 1874 +/- 167 to S101 123 +/- 147, which is consistent with zero. The all-sector figure confirms this: a clear flat-bottomed dip in S102, S11, S38, S99 and S100, a weak one in S65 and none in S101. The cutout depths are more consistent (cutout_sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.278, S102 r2.0 995 +/- 217 against QLP 1874), so the search depth of 1090.3 ppm looks inflated by detrending of the stellar variability. Depth beating between sectors fits a transit riding on pulsation as well as it fits a planet, and the present data cannot separate the two.

The other-sector evidence is weaker than predicted everywhere: other_sector_results gives S65 SNR 8.8 vs expected 12.9, S99 9.4 vs 13.0, S100 10.5 vs 14.8, S101 12.4 vs 14.4; joint_search_snr 8.4 (joint_search_detected True, joint_search_highest_null_snr 5.0) is below the single-sector S102 BLS SNR 12.3 in the record, as expected if the apparent depth varies between sectors.

Localisation supports the target but rests on two sectors: pixel_verdicts_by_sector gives S102 on target (SNR 7.3) and S100 unresolved (SNR 5.5, best star TIC 457325371); S11, S38, S65, S99 and S101 are too faint and the best star wanders among unrelated neighbours. The S102 and S100 difference images do peak on the target pixel, and joint_pixel_verdict is on target with joint_difference_image_snr 9.7 and joint_best_source TIC 457325371. The field is crowded (gaia_neighbours 176; 33 stars in gaia_neighbours_able_to_cause_dip, the closest Gaia DR3 6064573197263478784 at 12" G 17.6 needing 40%, and Gaia DR3 6064573197267811968 at 34" G 14.3 needing only 2%), which is the step 7 caution 'neighbour able to cause dip'; the pixel result makes a neighbour blend unlikely but not excluded in the faint sectors.

Evidence in favour that keeps this from a drop: triceratops_verdict likely planet with fpp_mean 0.0377 +/- 0.0012 and nfpp_mean 0 (nearby_scenarios_excluded True, most_likely_scenario TP on TIC 457325371); odd_even_difference_sigma 0.75; secondary_depth_ppm 160 +/- 68 below secondary_maximum_planet_depth_ppm 289, and the phase-0.5 panel of the all-sector figure shows no eclipse; gaia_rv_variable False with gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses 0.0494 from gaia_rv_nb_transits 21; gaia_ruwe 0.93, gaia_non_single_star 0, gaia_eclipsing_binary False; stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio 1.24 and fitted_to_expected_scaled_semi_major_axis 1.14.

The candidate is not a star by size: planet_radius_earth_radii 5.83 +/- 0.32 with transit_grazing False and fit_impact_parameter 0.388 +/- 0.2695, so the radius is constrained and well below 22.4 Earth radii (companion_radius_earth_radii 6.51328 from step 7 agrees). A 5.8 Earth-radius body at period_days 0.735 around a stellar_radius_solar_radii 1.85 star with gaia_vbroad_km_s 64 would be a rare ultra-short-period sub-Saturn, plausible but unusual enough that the pulsation question should be settled before submission.

No catalogue conflict: exofop_tois, exofop_ctois and published_signal are empty, ephemeris_match_likely_sources is empty, and released_tess_sectors_not_in_all_sector_verification is empty, so the signal would be new if it is real.

What would decide it: unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star 112 113 114 add three sectors for the per-sector depth test and the pixel check. If the dip recurs at fit_period_days 0.7349930 +/- 0.00000109 and fit_epoch_btjd 4077.68167 with depth near 863 ppm in all three sectors and the difference image again peaks on the target, propose for submission; if the depths again swing between about 0 and 1900 ppm, or the half-period modulation tracks the dip, propose for drop as a pulsation-driven false alarm. Sooner, a periodogram of the existing light curves showing whether a pulsation mode sits at 1/P or 2/P (about 1.36 or 2.72 cycles per day) would decide it.
